adds.rationale: GE Hitachi's contract award to BWXT to manufacture the reactor pressure vessel for the first BWRX-300 SMR is a concrete buildup-phase commercial milestone in the fission supply chain the profile is watching, distinct from the utility-scale SMR bets (SMR, OKLO) already held.

news_evidence.summary: GE Hitachi Nuclear Energy awards BWXT a contract to manufacture the reactor pressure vessel for the first BWRX-300 small modular reactor at Ontario Power Generation's Darlington New Nuclear Project; BWXT was first company in GEH's BWRX-300 qualified supplier group.

removes.rationale: Intuitive Machines' second consecutive Moon-landing mishap (IM-2's Athena lander tipped over and lost power within a day) repeats IM-1's 2024 tip-over, realizing the execution risk that was always the bear case and breaching the original commercialization thesis.

news_evidence.summary: Athena (IM-2) lander touches down on its side in a crater near the lunar south pole; contact issues, one antenna inoperative; mission declared over the next day as power depleted, though some NASA payload data was collected.

rationale_overall: One-for-one swap this quarter: LUNR exits on a repeated (second consecutive) lunar-landing execution failure that undercuts the near-term commercialization case for that specific ticker, while RKLB and ASTS continue to carry the rockets/spacecraft exposure (ASTS's March 3 FY2024 print showed a Vodafone commercial agreement and ~$1B pro forma cash). BWXT enters as a nuclear-supply-chain pure play on GE Hitachi's BWRX-300 SMR program, complementing SMR/OKLO/CCJ at the wave-bucket cap of four and adding a component-manufacturing angle distinct from the reactor developers and fuel supplier already held. Quantum (IONQ's Jan 6 Qubitekk close, RGTI's Ankaa-3 fidelity milestone, QBTS's March 'quantum supremacy' claim) and AI/defense/robotics/demographics holdings show continued milestone flow with no fundamental breach this quarter, so they are kept unchanged; net watchlist count stays at 22, under the 24 cap.
